mainTopic: נולד on יום טוב and the wick-cloth משנה: רבא's singed-wick reason, the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון over broken vessels, pits and shells, and רב המנונא's small-scrap explanation
overview: The גמרא continues discussing whether רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא in the wick משנה hold like רבי יהודה that נולד is forbidden on יום טוב. It shows that רב אדא בר אהבה was only explaining the תנאים and does not hold that way himself. רבא gives a different reason for רבי אליעזר: a wick that was not singed may not be lit. רב יוסף's 'exactly three by three' is then explained as a rule about טומאה. רב quotes the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about burning broken vessels, date pits and nutshells, and the גמרא explains why all three cases were needed. It then tells the story with רבי חייא that this teaching came from, and asks whether רב accepted it; the attempted proof is pushed off. The גמרא next shows how whole vessels can be burned according to רבי יהודה, by adding prepared wood following רב מתנה. Finally, רב המנונא explains that the משנה is about a scrap smaller than three by three handbreadths. Each sage follows his own view from a משנה in כלים, and all agree that a scrap thrown into the garbage is טהור.

steps.title: A ruling that seems to ignore נולד
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה: if a גוי carved a vessel out of a log on יום טוב, a Jew may burn it. It asks why this is allowed, since the vessel is נולד.
steps.simpleTranslation: A גוי who carved out a קב-sized vessel from a log — a Jew may burn it on יום טוב. But why? It is a newly created thing (נולד)!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא cites a ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה that seems to permit something נולד on יום טוב. It challenges this, because he had just explained the משנה according to רבי יהודה, who forbids נולד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the גוי carves the log, it stops being plain firewood and becomes a brand-new vessel on יום טוב. Something that came into existence on יום טוב is נולד, and according to רבי יהודה it is מוקצה. So permitting it to be burned appears to contradict רב אדא בר אהבה's own explanation of the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: a measure of volume; here, a vessel that holds a קב
a log or split piece of wood
something that newly came into being on שבת or יום טוב, and is therefore מוקצה

steps.confusionAlert: The ruling about the גוי is not a brand-new topic. It is quoted only to show a contradiction with רב אדא בר אהבה's explanation of the משנה, which had followed רבי יהודה.

phrases.english: A non-Jew who carved out a kav-sized vessel in a log —
a Jew may burn it on Yom Tov.
phrases.notes: This is the ruling of רב אדא בר אהבה.

phrases.english: But why? It is a newly-created thing!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אדא בר אהבה's earlier explanation that the משנה follows רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If he holds like רבי יהודה that נולד is forbidden, he should not permit burning a vessel newly carved on יום טוב.

steps.title: He was only explaining the תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה explained רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא according to their own view. He himself does not hold like רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said it according to the opinions of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא, but he himself does not hold that way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction. Explaining someone else's opinion is not the same as agreeing with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אדא בר אהבה's statement about the משנה was only an explanation of why רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא rule as they do: they hold like רבי יהודה on נולד. His own halachic view is that נולד is permitted on יום טוב. That is why he lets the carved vessel be burned.

keyTerms.meaning: according to their words or opinion
he does not hold this way

steps.whyThisMatters: A common גמרא move: an אמורא can explain a תנא's reasoning without accepting it as the הלכה.

phrases.english: According to the words of Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Akiva
he said it,
but he himself does not hold that way.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְדִבְרֵיהֶם דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא קָאָמַר לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction raised in step 1
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב אדא בר אהבה personally forbids נולד like רבי יהודה
steps.terutzMaskana: He only explained the תנאים that way; he personally permits נולד on יום טוב

steps.title: רבא's different reason for רבי אליעזר
steps.stepSummary: רבא says רבי אליעזר's reason has nothing to do with נולד. A wick or rag that was not singed before שבת may not be lit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: This is the reason of רבי אליעזר — because one may not light with a wick that was not singed, nor with rags that were not singed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא offers a whole new explanation of רבי אליעזר in the משנה, instead of the נולד explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבא, the problem is practical. An unsinged wick lights poorly, and that does not honor שבת properly. So רבי אליעזר's ruling about the folded cloth is not about the cloth changing status (נולד). It is about the cloth not being prepared to burn well.

phrases.english: Rava said,
this is the reason of Rabbi Eliezer:

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין מַדְלִיקִין בִּפְתִילָה שֶׁאֵינָהּ מְחוֹרֶכֶת
phrases.english: because one may not light with a wick that is not singed
nor with rags that are not singed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא אָמַר, הַיְינוּ טַעְמָא דְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an alternative to the נולד-based explanation of רבי אליעזר
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אליעזר forbids lighting the cloth because unsinged wicks and rags may not be lit on שבת

steps.title: Then why did רב יוסף stress 'exactly three by three'?
steps.stepSummary: If רבא is right, the exact size of the cloth does not matter. So what was the purpose of רב יוסף's teaching 'three by three exactly'?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then, that which רב יוסף taught, 'three by three exactly' — for what law is it relevant?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא. His explanation seems to make רב יוסף's precise size requirement pointless.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under the נולד explanation, the exact size mattered: a cloth of exactly three by three was a garment that could become טמא, and folding it into a wick made it a new thing. Under רבא's explanation, only singeing matters, so the size is irrelevant. The גמרא asks what רב יוסף's teaching is for.

keyTerms.meaning: but then, if so (introduces a difficulty)
three by three fingerbreadths, the minimum size of cloth that can become טמא
for what law is it relevant?

phrases.english: But then, that which Rav Yosef taught,
'three by three exactly'
for what law is it relevant?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב יוסף's precise measurement only makes sense if size matters, but in רבא's explanation it does not.

steps.title: רב יוסף was talking about טומאה
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף's teaching refers to the laws of טומאה, as seen in a משנה where רבי שמעון and חכמים disagree about whether the hem counts toward the size.
steps.simpleTranslation: It relates to ritual impurity. As we learned: The 'three by three' that they stated — excluding the hem, says רבי שמעון. And the Sages say: three by three exactly.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב יוסף's teaching is not connected to our משנה about wicks at all. It belongs to the laws of טומאה, and the גמרא quotes a משנה to show it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the משנה in כלים, רבי שמעון says the minimum three-by-three cloth is measured without the hem. חכמים say it must be exactly three by three, and the hem counts. רב יוסף's phrase 'exactly three by three' matches the חכמים in that טומאה dispute, so רבא's explanation still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: hem, the loose threads at the edge of a garment

steps.whatToRemember: רבא explains רבי אליעזר without נולד: an unsinged wick may not be lit. רב יוסף's 'exactly three by three' is moved to the laws of טומאה.

phrases.english: With regard to ritual impurity.
As we learned: The 'three by three' that they stated —

phrases.aramaic: חוּץ מִן הַמְּלָל, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן.
phrases.english: is excluding the hem; these are the words of Rabbi Shimon.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: שָׁלֹשׁ עַל שָׁלֹשׁ מְכֻוּוֹנוֹת.
phrases.english: And the Sages say: three by three exactly.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Relocating the source to a different halachic context
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב יוסף's measurement refers to the wick case and supports the נולד explanation
steps.terutzMaskana: רב יוסף's measurement refers to the laws of טומאה, following the חכמים against רבי שמעון

steps.title: רב quotes the dispute about burning broken or leftover items
steps.stepSummary: רב reports that רבי יהודה forbids burning broken vessels, date pits and nutshells on יום טוב as נולד, while רבי שמעון permits all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: One may burn with vessels but not with broken vessels — רבי יהודה; רבי שמעון permits. One may burn with dates, but once eaten, not with their pits — רבי יהודה; רבי שמעון permits. One may burn with nuts, but once eaten, not with their shells — רבי יהודה; רבי שמעון permits.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source of the dispute between רבי יהודה and רבי שמעון about נולד on יום טוב, using three cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In each case, something was fine to burn at the start of יום טוב but changed during the day: a vessel broke, or fruit was eaten and left pits or shells. רבי יהודה sees the changed item as נולד and forbids it. רבי שמעון does not consider this נולד and permits it.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the core תנאים dispute on נולד that the whole discussion about רבי יהודה's view depends on.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said that Rav said:
One may burn with vessels
but one may not burn with broken vessels;

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda. And Rabbi Shimon permits.
One may burn with dates;
if he ate them, one may not burn with their pits;

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda. And Rabbi Shimon permits.
One may burn with nuts;
if he ate them, one may not burn with their shells;

phrases.aramaic: דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה. וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן מַתִּיר.
phrases.english: these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda. And Rabbi Shimon permits.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the topic of נולד on יום טוב and gives the source of רבי יהודה's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה forbids burning broken vessels, date pits and nutshells on יום טוב as נולד; רבי שמעון permits

steps.title: Why the dates case was needed after the vessels case
steps.stepSummary: From vessels alone, we might think רבי יהודה forbids only when the item really changed, from a vessel to a broken one. Pits stayed pits, so we might have permitted them.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was necessary. For had he taught us only the first case, I would say רבי יהודה said it there because at first it was a vessel and now a broken vessel, so it is נולד and forbidden. But dates — at first there were pits and now there are pits — I would say it is fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why רב needed to list all three cases. It begins by showing what the dates case adds beyond the vessels case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A broken vessel is a clear change in identity, from a כלי to a שבר כלי. The pits were pits all along, so we might have thought there is no נולד there. The dates case teaches that רבי יהודה forbids even then.

keyTerms.meaning: and it was necessary (to teach every case)

phrases.english: And it was necessary.
For had he taught us the first case,
I would say that in that case Rabbi Yehuda says it,
because originally it was a vessel
and now it is a broken vessel,
so it is nolad, and forbidden.
But dates,
where originally there were pits and now there are pits —
I would say it is fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the necessity of the second case in רב's statement
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing each case teaches something new
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה forbids only a real change of identity, like a vessel breaking
steps.terutzMaskana: The dates case shows רבי יהודה forbids even when the item itself (the pit) did not change

steps.title: Why the nuts case was also needed
steps.stepSummary: From pits alone, we might think the problem is that pits were hidden and are now exposed. Nutshells were always exposed, so the nuts case was needed too. All three cases are necessary.
steps.simpleTranslation: And had he taught us only pits, I would have said: originally they were covered and now they are exposed. But nutshells — originally exposed and now exposed — I would say it is fine. It was necessary.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why each case is needed and concludes that all three were necessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pits changed in one way: they went from hidden inside the fruit to exposed, and that might count as נולד. Nutshells were visible from the start, with no change at all, yet רבי יהודה still forbids them. This shows how broadly רבי יהודה applies נולד.

keyTerms.meaning: I would have thought (a rejected initial assumption)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה treats as נולד anything that changed its usable state on יום טוב, even nutshells that were always visible. רבי שמעון permits all three cases.

phrases.english: And had he taught us only pits,
I would have said: originally they were covered
and now they are exposed.
But nutshells,
which originally were exposed and now are exposed —
I would say it is fine.
It was necessary.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the צריכותא begun in step 7
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: All three cases were needed: רבי יהודה forbids broken vessels, date pits and even always-visible nutshells as נולד, while רבי שמעון permits them all.

steps.title: רב's teaching came from a story, not an explicit statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא clarifies that רב's teaching about pits was inferred from an incident: רב threw date pits into an oven on a weekday, and רבי חייא told him the same act is forbidden on יום טוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב never said this teaching in so many words. It was learned from something that happened. רב ate dates on a weekday and threw the pits into the oven. רבי חייא said to him: 'Son of nobles, doing this same thing on יום טוב is forbidden.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds background to רב's teaching from Step 6. It tells us the teaching was learned from a story, and then it tells the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב did not state the rule about pits outright. It comes from רבי חייא's reaction when רב threw pits into an oven. This raises a new question, which comes in the next step: did רב himself agree with רבי חייא?

keyTerms.meaning: By inference, worked out from an action or a story
Son of nobles, a respectful way of addressing someone
The corresponding act, the same thing done at another time

steps.confusionAlert: רב threw the pits on a weekday, which is completely fine. רבי חייא was only warning him that doing the same thing on יום טוב would be forbidden.

phrases.english: And this teaching of Rav was not stated explicitly,
rather, it was stated by inference.
For Rav ate dates
and threw the pits into the oven.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא: בַּר פַּחֲתֵי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya said to him: Son of nobles,
the corresponding act on Yom Tov is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא דְּרַב לָאו בְּפֵירוּשׁ אִיתְּמַר, אֶלָּא מִכְּלָלָא אִיתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where רב's teaching from Step 6 came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule forbidding burning pits on יום טוב comes from רבי חייא's warning to רב, not from an explicit statement by רב.

steps.title: Did רב accept רבי חייא's ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב agreed with רבי חייא's ruling or not.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רב accept this from him, or did he not accept it from him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question: did רב agree with what רבי חייא told him? This sets up the attempted proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the teaching came from רבי חייא's words to רב, it is not clear that רב himself held this way. The גמרא wants to know רב's own opinion.

phrases.aramaic: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ אוֹ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ?
phrases.english: Did he accept it from him or did he not accept it from him?

steps.triggerLanguage: קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ אוֹ לָא קַבְּלַהּ מִינֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks a follow-up question about the story in Step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רב personally agreed that the pits are forbidden on יום טוב.

steps.title: Attempted proof that רב did not accept it
steps.stepSummary: When רב came to בבל, he threw date pits to animals on יום טוב. The גמרא suggests these were Persian dates, whose pits are bare, which would show that רב did not accept רבי חייא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: When רב came to בבל, he ate dates and threw the pits to the animals. Wasn't this with Persian dates, whose pits are completely clean? That would show רב did not accept רבי חייא's ruling.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second story about רב to try to answer the question. It suggests the story proves רב did not agree with רבי חייא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Persian dates come cleanly off the pit, so the bare pit is useless to people and should be מוקצה. If רב still handled and threw such pits on יום טוב, it seems he did not hold that they are forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Persian dates, whose fruit comes off the pit completely

phrases.aramaic: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב לְבָבֶל,
phrases.english: Come and hear: When Rav came to Babylonia,
he ate dates and threw the pits to the animals.
Was it not with Persian dates, and he did not accept it?
phrases.notes: Persian date pits have no fruit left on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּכִי אֲתָא רַב לְבָבֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries to answer the question from Step 10.
steps.raayaObject: That רב did not accept רבי חייא's ruling.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of רב in בבל throwing date pits to animals on יום טוב.

steps.title: No, these were Aramean dates with fruit still on the pits
steps.stepSummary: The proof is rejected. The dates were Aramean dates, whose pits still have fruit stuck to them. The pits may be handled because of the fruit on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it was with Aramean dates. Since the pits are still usable because of the fruit stuck to them, they may be handled.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from Step 11 by saying the story was about a different kind of date.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Aramean dates leave some fruit stuck to the pit. Because of that fruit, the pit is not a useless object, so handling it is allowed. The story therefore says nothing about bare pits, and רב may still have agreed with רבי חייא.

keyTerms.meaning: Aramean dates, whose fruit stays partly stuck to the pit
Because of their 'mother', meaning the fruit attached to them

phrases.english: No, it was with Aramean dates —
since they are fit for use because of their 'mother' (the fruit on them).

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof completely, leaving the question unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The proof assumed bare Persian date pits, but the story may involve Aramean dates with fruit still attached.

steps.title: How can whole vessels be burned if they quickly become broken?
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר בר חנה asks: according to רבי יהודה, whole vessels may be burned but broken ones may not. Once a vessel starts burning, it becomes broken pieces, so stirring the fire would mean handling forbidden pieces.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר בר חנה said to רב יוסף: According to רבי יהודה, who says one may burn whole vessels but not broken vessels, there is a problem. Once a vessel burns a little, it becomes broken pieces. So when one turns it over in the fire, is he not turning over something forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: A new challenge is raised against רבי יהודה's view: it seems impossible to burn whole vessels without ending up handling broken pieces.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה forbids broken vessel pieces because they are newly formed objects (נולד) on יום טוב. But burning a whole vessel soon breaks it, and stirring the fire then means moving those forbidden pieces. So permitting whole vessels seems useless in practice.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar bar Chana said to Rav Yosef:
According to Rabbi Yehuda, who said
one may kindle with vessels
and one may not kindle with broken vessels,
once he has ignited them a little,
they become broken vessels,

phrases.aramaic: וְכִי קָא מְהַפֵּךְ — בְּאִיסּוּרָא קָא מְהַפֵּךְ?
phrases.english: and when he turns them over — is he not turning over something forbidden?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר בַּר חָנָה לְרַב יוֹסֵף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new challenge to רבי יהודה's view from Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's ruling that whole vessels may be burned on יום טוב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A burning vessel quickly becomes broken pieces, which רבי יהודה forbids, so stirring the fire would involve handling forbidden items.

steps.title: Add prepared wood, following רב מתנה
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the person follows רב מתנה's method. Just as branches that fell into an oven on יום טוב may be burned by adding more prepared wood, here too one adds permitted wood so the forbidden pieces are only a minority.
steps.simpleTranslation: He acted like רב מתנה taught. רב מתנה said in the name of רב: If branches fell from a palm tree into an oven on יום טוב, one adds more wood that was prepared before יום טוב, and then he may burn them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 13 by bringing a method from רב מתנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Branches that fell off a tree on יום טוב are מוקצה. But if one adds more permitted wood, the forbidden branches become a minority and one may stir the fire. The same works for broken vessel pieces, so רבי יהודה's ruling is workable.

keyTerms.meaning: Branches or wood that fell off

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, whole vessels may be burned on יום טוב. The problem of their turning into broken pieces is solved by adding enough prepared wood that the forbidden pieces are a minority.

phrases.english: Where he acted in accordance with Rav Mattana.
For Rav Mattana said in the name of Rav:
Branches that fell from a palm tree
into an oven on Yom Tov,
he adds prepared wood and kindles them.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a practical method from another אמורא's ruling.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Burning whole vessels must lead to handling forbidden broken pieces.
steps.terutzMaskana: Adding prepared wood makes the forbidden pieces a minority, so the fire may be stirred.

steps.title: רב המנונא: the משנה is about a cloth smaller than three by three
steps.stepSummary: רב המנונא gives a different explanation of the cloth-wick משנה: it deals with a cloth smaller than three by three טפחים (handbreadths), and it teaches the lenient rules for small scraps of cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב המנונא said: Here we are dealing with a cloth smaller than three by three. The משנה here is teaching the lenient rules about small scraps of cloth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the cloth-wick משנה and brings רב המנונא's different way of explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier explanations focused on a cloth of three by three and whether its size or purpose matters. רב המנונא says the משנה is about a smaller piece, so the argument there is about the lenient rules that apply to small scraps of cloth.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three (טפחים, handbreadths), the normal minimum size of cloth that can become טמא
Small scraps or patches of cloth

steps.whyThisMatters: This changes the case of the משנה: the debate is not about a full-size cloth but about small scraps, which have special lenient rules.

phrases.english: Rav Hamnuna said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with less than three by three,
they taught here from the leniencies of small cloths.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב הַמְנוּנָא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּפָחוֹת מִשְּׁלֹשָׁה עַל שְׁלֹשָׁה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the cloth discussion before Step 6 and offers a different explanation of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's dispute concerns a cloth smaller than three by three and teaches the leniencies of small scraps.

steps.title: Each sage follows his own known opinion
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא states that רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא in our wick משנה are each consistent with views they hold elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אליעזר follows his own reasoning, and רבי עקיבא follows his own reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that the dispute in our משנה matches another dispute between the same two sages. This line sets up the next step, where the גמרא will quote the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב המנונא said our משנה is about a scrap smaller than three by three טפחים (handbreadths). The גמרא now says this fits well with how רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא rule about such small scraps in general. Their positions in our משנה are not new. Each one is applying a rule he already holds.

keyTerms.meaning: According to his own reasoning; consistent with his known view

phrases.english: And Rabbi Eliezer follows his own reasoning
and Rabbi Akiva follows his own reasoning

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָזְדָא רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר לְטַעְמֵיהּ וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא לְטַעְמֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on רב המנונא's explanation by linking it to a known dispute
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The positions of רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא in the wick משנה match their positions on small cloth scraps elsewhere.

steps.title: The משנה in כלים about small cloth scraps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה in which רבי אליעזר, רבי יהושע and רבי עקיבא argue about whether a small scrap set aside for cleaning jobs can become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: A scrap smaller than three by three טפחים (handbreadths) that someone set aside to plug the bathhouse drain, to lift a hot pot, or to wipe the millstone can become טמא, whether or not it was kept ready for that purpose. These are the words of רבי אליעזר. רבי יהושע says: Whether or not it was kept ready, it is טהור. רבי עקיבא says: If it was kept ready, it is טמא. If it was not kept ready, it is טהור.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source that shows each sage's general view about small scraps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A scrap smaller than three by three טפחים (handbreadths) is too small to count as a real garment. The question is whether being used for a job gives it enough importance to become טמא. רבי אליעזר says yes, always. רבי יהושע says no, never. רבי עקיבא says only if it was specially kept ready for the job. This explains our משנה: רבי אליעזר says the wick-scrap is still טמא, while רבי עקיבא says a scrap that was not specially readied is טהור.

keyTerms.meaning: Three by three (טפחים, handbreadths), the minimum size of a meaningful cloth
Prepared, specially kept ready for the job
Can become ritually impure / cannot become ritually impure

steps.confusionAlert: Here טָהוֹר does not mean 'clean right now.' It means the scrap cannot become טמא at all, because it is not considered a significant item.

phrases.english: As we learned in a mishna:
A cloth smaller than three by three handbreadths
that one set aside to plug the bathhouse with it
and to lift (pour from) the pot with it
and to wipe the millstone with it
whether it was prepared
or whether it was not prepared
it can become impure; these are the words of Rabbi Eliezer.
And Rabbi Yehoshua says:
Whether it was prepared
or whether it was not prepared, it is pure.
Rabbi Akiva says:
If it was prepared, it is impure;
and if it was not prepared, it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the source for the claim that each sage follows his own reasoning
steps.raayaObject: That רבי אליעזר and רבי עקיבא in the wick משנה are consistent with their general views
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה in מסכת כלים about small scraps used for plugging, lifting a pot, and wiping a millstone

steps.title: Everyone agrees a scrap thrown in the garbage is טהור
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoted by עולא or רבה בר בר חנה, says that all three sages agree that a small scrap thrown into the garbage cannot become טמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say it was רבה בר בר חנה, in the name of רבי יוחנן: Everyone agrees that if a person threw the scrap into the garbage dump, it is טהור according to all opinions.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a point of agreement: even רבי אליעזר admits that a small scrap thrown into the garbage is טהור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר said a small scrap is always טמא, prepared or not. רבי יוחנן limits that: once the owner throws the scrap away, he has shown it has no value to him, so even רבי אליעזר agrees it is טהור. This sets a boundary. רבי אליעזר's view applies only to scraps the owner still keeps and values.
steps.whatToRemember: For scraps under three by three טפחים (handbreadths): רבי אליעזר says always טמא, רבי יהושע says always טהור, and רבי עקיבא says טמא only if prepared. But once the scrap is thrown in the garbage, all agree it is טהור.
steps.whyThisMatters: Throwing something away shows that the owner no longer values it, and that removes its importance for טומאה. This idea will matter when the גמרא looks at how a wick-scrap compares to a discarded one.

phrases.english: And Ulla said,
and some say it was Rabba bar bar Ḥana,
who said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan:
Everyone agrees that if one threw it into the garbage,
according to all opinions it is pure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the dispute in the כלים משנה by adding a case where all sages agree
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A small scrap thrown into the garbage is טהור according to everyone, even רבי אליעזר.
